IRCC Levels Plans set permanent-resident targets; StatCan measures population growth and temporary-resident stocks; IRCC publishes inventory/backlog figures. Housing, health, and education capacity are separate provincial/municipal systems. “Open borders” and “policy malpractice” are political frames — intake and backlog numbers are not.
On the record: levels, temporary stocks, backlogs, housing starts, health attachment rates.

Inference (labeled): rapid intake without matching housing and health capacity produces stress. That is a planning critique, not a claim that immigration itself is illegitimate. Canada remains an immigrant nation by history and law.
